09_marg239: AND [THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL] DID. ADAMANTIUS. The Madianites are not said to have prevailed over the people of God while it kept the commandments. When, then, it began to neglect them, the enemy at once prevailed. Against us too, who are called Israel according to the spirit, the spiritual enemy rises up when we neglect the commandments of God; and we are delivered to the enemies when we are forsaken by the grace of God.
09_interl404: "He that soweth in the flesh, of the flesh also shall reap corruption"
09_marg240: AND WHEN [ISRAEL] HAD SOWN. ADAMANTIUS. Israel according to the flesh suffered these things. It sowed the land, but because it had been delivered to its enemies for its sins, it reaped corruption instead of crops. But we, who are named Israel according to the spirit, sometimes sow, and the enemies cannot spoil what is sown nor lie in wait for our husbandry. But there is a time when our sowings are spoiled. Whence: He that soweth in the flesh, of the flesh also shall reap corruption; but he that soweth in the spirit, of the spirit shall reap life everlasting. The Madianites, then, spoil the seeds of those who sow in the flesh, and their fruits are destroyed and perish. But what is sown in the spirit the Madianites cannot spoil. For the demons cannot go up to the spiritual fields and violate the fallow lands of the spirit, namely of those who do not sow upon thorns, but break up for themselves fallow ground.
09_marg241: It often happens too that one who, toiling much in spiritual work, has brought forth very many fruits, and has filled his barns with the crop of justice, and has laid up many good works in the chamber of his conscience, yet, if he grows negligent and after his labour inclines more readily to pleasure, all those seeds of good things will be spoiled, lust having the mastery. Therefore it is said: With all watchfulness keep thy heart. The heart, therefore, is to be kept from every sin, especially in time of persecution. For if anyone then denies the faith, he has lost all the fruits of justice, made suddenly naked and empty; and what was long sought and gathered with much and hardly won labour, all that labour is suddenly poured out, according to that: All his justices which he hath done shall not be remembered. Let us pray, then, that we may be able to endure persecution, because tribulation worketh patience, and patience trial, and trial hope. For our trial extends not only to stripes, but even to the shedding of blood, because Christ, whom we follow, shed his blood for our redemption, that we might go forth thence washed in our own blood. For the baptism of blood alone is that which renders us purer than the water of baptism, of which it is said: I have a baptism wherewith I am to be baptized, which you know not. He called, then, the shedding of his blood a baptism. And if I do not offend in teaching these things, I fear that this baptism is more eminent than that baptism which is given through water. For of those who receive that one, very few keep it unspotted to the end of life; but he who has been baptized with this can sin no more. And if it is not rash to hear something in such matters, we can say that by that baptism past sins are purged, by this future ones too are destroyed. And the prince of this world, coming to such a soul, finds nothing; nay, he is lulled by the shedding of blood, and dares not accuse in anything the soul made glorious by its death, washed in blood.
09_marg242: AND HE SENT UNTO THEM, etc. AUGUSTINE. Why the name of this prophet is not given, the cause is hidden; yet I do not think there is none. But because after the words with which he reproached the people for disobedience, the Scripture follows, saying: And an angel of the Lord came and sat under the oak that was in Ephra, it is not absurdly understood that this angel was signified by the name of a man, so that after he had spoken these words he came to the oak and sat there. For angels are often spoken of by the name of men; but that angels are called prophets does not come to mind, though one who is a prophet is often found to be called an angel. But if prophetic sayings of angels are known, that is, by which they foretold things to come, why could not an angel be called a prophet?
09_interl405: in the shade of the oak, that is, of the cross
09_marg243: AND WHEN GEDEON. ISIDORE. Gedeon signifies Christ, who, set under the shade of the holy cross, in the predestined mystery of the incarnation to come, by the rectitude of judgment as with a rod separated the election of the saints from the chaff of the vices.
09_interl408: AUGUSTINE. He speaks with the authority of the Lord by whom he was sent
09_interl409: because the devil "transformeth himself into an angel of light"
09_marg244: GIVE ME A SIGN. ADAMANTIUS. A learned man, and having the example of Jesus his predecessor, he acts more cautiously. For he knew that the angels of darkness can transform themselves into angels of light; therefore he tries the spirit, whether it be of God. For the spiritual man examines all things. So his predecessor Jesus Nave, when he had seen the prince of the heavenly host, asks: Art thou ours or of our adversaries? Therefore Gedeon tests the angelic vision by the diversity and change of signs.
09_marg245: AND BRING A SACRIFICE. AUGUSTINE. It is to be noted that Gedeon does not say to the angel: I will offer thee a sacrifice, but: I will offer my sacrifice, and lay it before thee. Whence it is to be understood that he offered the sacrifice not to the angel but through the angel. Which the angel showed, who did not take it from him as for himself, but said to him: Take the flesh and the unleavened loaves and lay them upon that rock, and pour out the broth. And when he had done this, the angel of the Lord put forth the tip of the rod that was in his hand and touched the flesh and the unleavened loaves, etc. So the angel himself fulfilled in the sacrifice the office of one ministering. For the fire which a human minister would have set under it without a miracle, as a man, he himself set under it wonderfully, as an angel. Then at last Gedeon knew that he was an angel of the Lord. For the Scripture adds this at once: And Gedeon saw that he was an angel of the Lord. Before, then, he was speaking as with a man, whom yet he believed to be a man of God, so that he wished to offer the sacrifice before him, as if to be helped by the presence of his holiness.
09_marg246: SO GEDEON WENT IN. GREGORY. Gedeon, while he was threshing the wheat from the chaff, saw an angel, at whose command he boiled a kid, put it on the rock, and poured the broth of the flesh over it. These the angel touched with his rod, and fire coming out of the rock consumed them. To beat the wheat with a rod is, by the rectitude of judgment, to separate the grains of the virtues from the chaff of the vices. To those who do this an angel appears, because the Lord makes known inward things the more, the more zealously men cleanse themselves from outward things. He commands the kid to be killed, that is, every appetite of our flesh to be sacrificed, and the flesh to be put upon the rock, and the broth of the flesh to be poured over it. The rock signifies Christ, of whom it is said: And the rock was Christ. We put the flesh upon the rock when we crucify our body in imitation of Christ. He also pours the broth of the flesh over it who in the conversation of Christ has emptied out even his carnal thoughts themselves. For it is as if the broth melted from the flesh were poured upon the rock when the mind is emptied of the flow of carnal thoughts. That the angel touches with the rod is because the power of the divine help does not forsake our intention. Fire comes out of the rock and consumes the broth and the flesh, because the spirit breathed from the Redeemer burns our heart with so great a flame of compunction that it burns up all that is unlawful in it of work and thought. For the perfect mind watches carefully, not only to refuse to do perverse things, but also to wipe away all that basely melts in it through thoughts.
09_interl410: every appetite, namely, of the flesh
09_marg247: SO GEDEON WENT IN, etc. AND PRESENTED TO HIM, etc. AUGUSTINE. It is asked why Gedeon dared to offer a sacrifice apart from the place where God had commanded. For he forbade sacrifice to be made to him outside his tabernacle, to which the temple succeeded. And in the time of Gedeon the tabernacle was in Silo. But it is to be known that he at first thought the angel a prophet, and consulted him about offering a sacrifice to the Lord. If he had forbidden it, it would not have been done. But because he assented, Gedeon followed the authority of God. For God so established those legal ordinances as to give laws not to himself but to men. Whence what he himself commanded apart from them was fulfilled not by transgressors but by the obedient, as by Abraham in sacrificing his son. So Elias sacrificed outside the tabernacle of the Lord, to convince the priests of the idols, by the command of the Lord, who bade him do this by revelation and inspiration. And yet the custom of sacrificing apart from the tabernacle had grown so frequent that even Solomon is found to have sacrificed on the high places, and his sacrifice was not rejected. And yet those kings are censured who among their praiseworthy works did not destroy the high places, where against the law of God the people had been wont to sacrifice; and he who destroyed them is the more praised. Thus God bore with, rather than forbade, the custom of his people by which, though apart from his tabernacle, they offered not to strange gods but to their own God, hearing those who offered even so. But what Gedeon did was brought about through the angel, that it might be done prophetically, so that in the prophecy that rock might be set forth; to which sacrifice was not offered, but from which fire is recorded to have come out to consume the sacrifice. For whether by the water which the rock poured forth when struck in the desert, or by fire, the gift of the Holy Ghost is signified, which Christ has poured out most richly upon us. Whence: "If any man thirst, let him come and drink. He that believeth in me, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water. Now this he said of the Spirit which they should receive who believed in him." And elsewhere: There appeared to them parted tongues as it were of fire, etc. And the Lord himself says: I am come to cast fire on the earth.
09_interl413: Christ, in imitation of whom we crucify our body
09_interl414: the spirit, namely, breathed from the Redeemer
09_interl415: ISIDORE. Because in the flesh of Christ the sins of the whole world were blotted out, [the rock] namely struck with the rod, that is, crucified; and it purged not only deeds but also desires. For the flesh of the kid signifies the guilt of the deed, the broth the allurements of desire. The fire went out of the rock because the flesh of Christ, filled with the divine Spirit, burned up all sins; whence: "I am come to cast fire on the earth", etc.
09_marg248: AND THOU SHALT TAKE THE BULLOCK. ISIDORE. The one which his father had assigned to the idols Gedeon killed, and he sacrificed another of seven years to God. In which he shows that after the coming of Christ all the sacrifices of heathenism are to be abolished, and now only the sacrifice of the passion of Christ is to be offered to God for the redemption of the people. For he is the bullock of seven years, full, namely, of the sevenfold Spirit.
09_interl417: ISIDORE. Going about in the womb: this is Christ, who, incarnate in the womb of the Virgin, was within the womb
09_interl418: that is, strong against Baal through the substance of weakness, and outside the world through the power of majesty
09_interl421: a licking people, that is, given to the belly and the gullet
09_interl422: ADAMANTIUS. The Seventy: the sons of the east, that is, false Christians
09_marg249: NOW ALL. ADAMANTIUS. There came together against Israel the Madianites, who are interpreted outside judgment, who, namely, are outside the judgment of God, and have sinned without the law and shall perish without the law; and Amalec, that is, a licking people, an earthly nation, namely, given to the belly and the gullet: carnal Israel, namely, came together against the spiritual. The sons of the east too are mixed with them. For every one who takes upon himself the name of Christ is made a son of the east. For of Christ it is said: Behold a man, the Orient is his name. But not always do those who have the name of Christ remain in the Church of Christ. When the heretics, who are reckoned by the name of Christ, assail the Church and the faith, the sons of the east with the Madianites and Amalec assail the people of God, with the pagans, namely, and the Jews.
09_interl423: ADAMANTIUS. In low and humble places, namely, do they pitch their camp who wish to assail the people of God.
09_marg250: IN THE VALLEY OF JEZRAEL. ADAMANTIUS. Which is interpreted the seed of God. For the adversaries do not dare to go there where the fruits of the spirit are already born, but where the seed of God still lies and the fruit has not yet come up. For some fell by the wayside, and the birds of the air snatch it away; these, namely, are they who hear the word of God and receive it with joy; but the devil comes and takes away the word, or seed, out of their heart. So, then, these come and seek to take away the seed of God from the heart of those in whom it is sown, because they find them set in the valleys and following low things. For they receive the word of God lowly and unworthily and with a Jewish understanding. But he who goes up from the lowness of the letter to the heights of the spirit, from him the Madianites or Amalecites snatch nothing, nor the sons of the east either, because he is set on the summit of spiritual understanding.
09_interl424: The Seventy: The Spirit of the Lord strengthened Gedeon
09_interl425: "The spirit of wisdom and of understanding, the spirit of counsel and of fortitude", etc., filled him
09_interl426: ADAMANTIUS. The Seventy: And he called Abiezer after him; who, namely, was nowhere. And it is interpreted 'the help of our father'; he seems, then, to have called not some man but the help of the most high Father.
09_interl427: ISIDORE. He did not ask this sign as one unbelieving, but foresaw the mysteries to come and diligently searches them out, that he may believe the mystery the more when he has understood the oracle.
09_interl429: where the harvest is to be cleansed and the chaff separated from the wheat
09_interl430: of the whole world, namely, in which the superstition of the Gentiles was parched in its fruitless worship
09_interl431: of the word of God, which was given in the time of the law
09_interl432: because no moisture of the divine word watered the other nations
09_marg251: IF THOU WILT SAVE. If thou wilt save Israel by my hand, as thou hast said, behold I will put a fleece of wool on the floor, etc. Since there are many and innumerable signs which he could have asked to confirm the promise, it is asked why, after the angelic voice and the heavenly promise, he asked this new sign; [and,] having obtained it, he wrings the fleece into a basin; [and] why, in reversed order, he asks a second sign; especially since it is said: "Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God." But the issue of the matter teaches that it was not done against the commandment. For God would not have granted the petition if it had been against the law. The reason, then, of this mystery is to be seen. Now I remember that one of our predecessors said that the fleece of wool is the people of Israel; and the rest of the ground the rest of the nations; and the dew which fell upon the fleece the word of God, which was sent from heaven to that people alone. For the dew of the divine law had come upon Israel only; but dryness held all the nations, which no moisture of the divine word watered.
09_marg252: ON THE FLOOR. THE SAME. Not just anywhere, not in a field nor in a woodland, but on the floor, where the harvest is. The harvest indeed is great, but the labourers are few. He foresaw by the Holy Ghost that Christ gathers his people on the floor and cleanses it there, holding the fan in his hand. Not without cause, then, did so great and such a man, of whom even the Apostle makes mention in the catalogue of the prophets, choose the floor for laying the fleece. Nor without cause did he wring the fleece into a basin and fill it with water. For Christ laid aside his garments and, girding himself with a towel, put water into a basin and washed the feet of the disciples. Thou seest, then, that the prophets foreshadowed these things which were to be fulfilled in the last times through Christ. The water put into the basin, then, was the dew of heavenly grace, with which the feet of the disciples are washed. Whence he says: Now you are clean by reason of the word which I have spoken to you.
09_marg253: But we too, if we offer our feet, Jesus is ready to wash the feet of our soul and to cleanse them with the heavenly dew, the grace of the Holy Ghost, the word of doctrine. For he willed not the apostles only to be clean, but also all who believe through his word; and he says to all with Peter: If I wash thee not, thou shalt have no part with me. For no one has part with Jesus unless washed and clean. Lay aside, I pray, O Lord, the garments which thou didst put on for me; gird thyself for me; put water into a basin, and wash the feet of thy servants; wash away the filth of thy sons and daughters; wash the feet of our soul, that, imitating and following thee, we may put off the old garments, saying: I have put off my garment, how shall I put it on? I have washed my feet, how shall I defile them? For when thou hast washed my feet, thou wilt at once make me sit at table with thee and hear: You call me Master and Lord, and you say well, for so I am, etc. I will, then, wash the feet of my brethren. Therefore I draw water from the fountains of Israel; nay, I wring it out of the Israelite fleece, now from the fleece of the book of Judges or the book of Kings, now from the fleece of Isaias or Jeremias; and I put it into the basin of my soul, conceiving the sense in my heart, and I take the feet of those who offer themselves to be washed, that, all purified by the word, we may not be cast out of the bridal chamber for filthy garments, but with white garments, washed feet and clean heart, may sit at the banquet of the bridegroom Jesus Christ.
09_marg254: IF THERE BE DEW ON THE WHOLE FLEECE. AUGUSTINE. In the trial of Gedeon the Lord showed what he wished to foretell: namely, that the fleece rained upon, with the whole floor round about dry, figures the first people of Israel, among whom were the saints with heavenly grace, as with a spiritual rain; and that afterwards the floor rained upon, with the fleece dried, figures the Church of God spread through the whole world, having heavenly grace not in a fleece, as in a veil, but in the open, the former people being as it were estranged from the dew of the same grace and dried up.
09_interl434: Christ "put water into a basin, and washed the feet of the disciples"
09_interl435: with the sense of the word
09_interl439: When, namely, the sheep of the house of Israel shall have perished and denied the fountain of living water, let the dew of faith dry up in the sinners of the Jews.
09_marg255: I PRAY THAT THE FLEECE ONLY, etc. ADAMANTIUS. In the reason of the second sign too, in which he says that the dew should come down upon all the ground, but dryness remain upon the fleece: see all this people, which has been gathered from the Gentiles through all the earth, having now the divine dew in itself, and filled within with dew, and watered by the writings of the prophets, and growing green with the evangelical moisture; but that fleece, that is, the Jewish people, suffering the dryness of the word of God, according to that: The children of Israel shall sit many days without king, without prince, without prophet, etc. The Prophet too, describing the coming of Christ, says: He shall come down like rain upon the fleece, and as showers falling gently upon the earth. For Christ came down like rain upon the fleece of the people of the circumcision, and as showers falling upon the earth, that is, upon the rest of the earth; but dropping also upon us, and bringing to us Gentiles the drops of the heavenly dew, that we too might drink, who were upon the earth dried up with continual drought. Holy Gedeon, then, beholding this order of the mystery with the prophetic spirit, asks the second sign too in reversed order. For he knew that the divine dew, which is the coming of the Son of God, would be not only for the Jews but afterwards for the Gentiles also, because by the unbelief of Israel salvation comes to the Gentiles. And this is why, instead of the dryness of the fleece, the whole earth is watered with the grace of the divine dew.
09_interl440: In human wars a more numerous army affords safer help, but it is not so in divine ones. For the work of divine power is not clear if it is propped by human supports. "The king is not saved by a great army."

09_interl442: As if: let him leave the contests to brave men, lest he give the rest an example of fear and dread.
09_marg256: WHOSOEVER IS FEARFUL AND TIMOROUS. ADAMANTIUS. Jesus cries the same today: He that is fearful and timorous of heart, let him not come to me to the wars. For he says: He that taketh not up his cross and followeth me is not worthy of me; and: He that hateth not his father and mother, brothers, sisters and children, yea and his own life also, is not worthy of me. Again: He that doth not renounce all that he possesseth cannot be my disciple. So he separates the fearful and timorous from his camp. Let the soldier of Christ, then, drive out fear and dread, and say confidently: If armies in camp should stand together against me, my heart shall not fear; and: The Lord is my light and my salvation, whom shall I fear? etc. Let not this malice frighten you, which is easily overcome by those who serve faithfully. In this camp women are wont to conquer, not by strength of body but by the power of faith, like Debbora, and Judith, who restored to her country the safety which the men had lost. Virgins too in their first youth have borne the tortures of tyrants for martyrdom. In those, then, who serve God, strength not of body but of soul is sought, because the victory is won not with darts of iron but with the weapons of prayers, and faith in the contest gives endurance. Whence: Stand therefore, having on the breastplate of justice, having your loins girt about with truth; and take the helmet of salvation and the sword of the Spirit; in all things the shield of faith, etc. So armed we ought to take up the standards of the cross of Christ and follow him. Yet if in persecution thou seest thyself inferior in strength to the cruelty of the tyrant, it is [permitted] in the service of Christ to give place to wrath, to flee from place to place; nor is a military offence charged to thee in this. Whence: If they persecute you in one city, flee into another. For the sum of the matter is not to deny Jesus, whom thou hast once confessed. And he confesses who flees for this reason, that he may not deny. In the Apocalypse, when those are enumerated who are to be cast into the pool of fire with the unbelievers and fornicators and sorcerers, the fearful and timorous are counted. So among great and abominable crimes the crime of fear and dread is set.
09_marg257: THE SEVENTY. He is fearful who, as from a growing vice, is terrified by thought alone before he sees evils, rolling a chill dread through his limbs, so that he is undone not so much by the sight of evils as by hearing and expecting them. Therefore according to the Seventy he is called fearful of heart; for this vice remains fixed in the heart and in the inner parts of the mind. But he is timorous who trembles at the first sight of the encounter, yet is not terrified with his whole heart, but can be restored and given courage again.
09_interl443: the catechumens, namely, who give way in terror before baptism
09_marg258: THE PEOPLE ARE STILL. ADAMANTIUS. The people are still many; bring them down to the water, and there I will try them for thee. As I see, those who were first rejected had not even gone down into the water, but still showed themselves catechumens, and were so deterred by the vice of dread that they did not even go down to the saving laver. Therefore they were rejected. But these second ones come to the water, to be tried there. And the Lord said to Gedeon: Every one that shall lap the water with his tongue, as a dog lappeth, thou shalt set him apart, etc. In almost all the deeds of the ancients great mysteries are signified, as here. For those who go down to the water, that is, to the grace of baptism, must not go forward on to the ground, nor bend the knees and yield to the temptations to come, but stand constantly, and lift up the hands that hang down and the feeble knees, and make straight steps with their feet. Thou hast come to the water of baptism; this is for thee the beginning of the spiritual fight. If thou art slack, if thou canst easily be bent, how wilt thou fight? How wilt thou stand against the wiles of the devil? Therefore the Apostle cries: Stand fast, and be not held again under the yoke of bondage. He, then, is approved, he is chosen, who, after he has come to the waters of baptism, knows not how to be bent to bodily and earthly necessities, who does not indulge vices, nor is laid prone through the thirst of sin.

09_marg259: THEY THAT WITH HAND AND TONGUE. He says that they lap the water with hand and tongue, because the soldiers of Christ ought to work with hand and tongue, that is, with work and word. For he that shall do and teach shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven. He brings in too the likeness of the dog lapping, because above all other animals it is said to keep love for its own master, and its affection is said not to be blotted out either by terror or by injuries. There are, then, three hundred only who bear the image of this sacrament. These are the chosen, the approved, and the consecrated for victory, who can overcome the adversaries even by the very sacrament of the number. For they are three hundred, who are multiplied by three hundreds, and bear the number of the perfect Trinity.

09_marg260: AND THE NUMBER WAS. AUGUSTINE. And the number of those who lapped with their hand, with their tongue, was three hundred men. Most Latin codices do not have with their hand, but only with their tongue, because they so understood what was said above, as dogs. But the Greek has both, with their hand, with their tongue, that it may be understood that they cast into the mouth water caught up with the hand, like dogs, which do not draw the water they drink with the mouth applied, as oxen do, but snatch it into the mouth with the tongue; as these too did, but casting the water into the mouth with the hand, which they received with the tongue. And the translation from the Hebrew has this more plainly: And the number of them that had lapped water, casting it with the hand to their mouth, was three hundred men. For men do not drink so as to draw water with the tongue without the work of the hand, like dogs; nor indeed had these been commanded to do this; but when they had gone down to the water to drink, many drank on bended knee, because it was done more easily and with less labour. But a few did not bend the knee but stooped, and drank like dogs, the water cast into the mouth with the hand. Their number, because they were three hundred, signifies the cross, because of the Greek letter tau. By which too it was prefigured that the Gentiles would rather believe in Christ crucified, because it is a Greek letter. Whence the Apostle signifies all the Gentiles by the name of the Greeks, saying: "To the Jew first, and to the Greek"; because among the tongues of the Gentiles the Greek so excels that all are fittingly signified by it. This number is to be noticed also in the home-born servants of Abraham, by whom he set free his brother from the enemy, when Melchisedech blessed him in a great mystery. For what is over, the eighteen, seems to signify at what time it would be done, that is, in the third, which was to be under grace. For the first is before the law, the second under the law, the third under grace. And the single times are signified by the number six, because of its perfection; for three sixes are eighteen. Whence too the woman who had been in infirmity eighteen years, bent over, the Saviour raised up. And that these were so approved that they were said to be like dogs in drinking signifies that God chose the contemptible and the ignoble; for the dog is held in contempt. Whence: It is not good to take the bread of the children and to cast it to the dogs. David too calls himself a dog, as something contemptible.
09_interl452: because "praise is not seemly in the mouth of a sinner"
09_interl453: AUGUSTINE. Because through the contemptible things of the world the Saviour confounded his enemies
09_marg261: IT STRUCK IT, AND BEAT IT DOWN. GREGORY. Of this battle it is said through the Prophet: "Thou hast overcome the yoke of their burden, and the rod of their shoulder, and the sceptre of their oppressor, as in the day of Madian." For the Lord, rescuing the Gentiles, overcame the yoke of their burden when by his coming he set them free from the servitude of the devil. He overcame the rod of their shoulder when, the human race being redeemed, he checked his smiting, which pressed them down heavily from perverse work. He overcame the sceptre of their oppressor when he cast down from the heart of the faithful the kingdom of the devil, who exacted the tributes of punishment due for sins. The coming of the Redeemer, then, is compared to the victory of this fight, because it is signified in that victory of Gedeon. For Gedeon signifies the coming of the Redeemer, of whom it is said: Lift up your gates, O ye princes, and be ye lifted up, O eternal gates, and the King of glory shall enter in; the Lord who is strong and mighty, the Lord mighty in battle. This Gedeon prophesied by deed and by name: for Gedeon is interpreted going round in the womb. For Christ by the power of his majesty went round all things, but by the grace of his dispensation came into the womb of the Virgin; who, redeeming us by his dispensation, embracing all things by his divinity and taking humanity within the womb, was incarnate in the womb and was not shut in, because he was within the womb by the substance of weakness, and outside the world by the power of majesty. And Madian is interpreted from judgment: for his enemies were driven back not from the judgment of him who drives back, but from the judgment of him who judges justly. Therefore they are called from judgment, because, being strangers to the grace of the Redeemer, they bear even in their name the desert of just damnation. Against these Gedeon goes to battle with three hundred. In the hundred the fulness of perfection is wont to be understood. What, then, in the three hundred but the perfect knowledge of the Trinity? For with these the Lord destroys the adversaries of the faith, with these he goes down to the wars of preaching, who can know divine things and think perfectly of the Trinity, which is God. And it is to be noted that the number three hundred is contained in the letter tau, and is marked by the figure of the cross; which holds the figure of the cross, to which, if what stands out above in the cross were added to the cross line, it would be no longer the figure of the cross but the cross itself. Because, then, this number is contained in the letter tau, and by it shows the figure of the cross, rightly in these three hundred following Gedeon are signified those to whom it is said: If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me. They who follow the Lord take up the cross the more truly, the more keenly they both tame themselves and are tormented with the compassion of charity toward their neighbours. Whence: "Mark tau upon the foreheads of the men that sigh and mourn." Or by the three hundred this is signified, that the iron of the enemies is overcome by the wood of the cross.
09_marg262: AND HE DIVIDED THE THREE HUNDRED. They were led to the river to drink the waters, and those who drew them on bended knees were removed from the purpose of the war. For by the waters the doctrine of wisdom is signified, and by the knee standing upright right working. Those, then, who bend the knee while they drink the waters are kept from the war, because Christ goes to battle against the enemies of the faith with those who, while they draw in doctrine, do not bend the rightness of works. For all are related to have drunk water then, but not all to have stood with upright knee; and those were rejected who bent their knees in drinking, because not the hearers of the law are just before God, but the doers. For because slackness of works is signified by the bending of the knees, it is rightly said: Lift up the hands which hang down and the feeble knees, and make straight steps with your feet. They go forth, then, to war with Christ as leader who show by work what they proclaim with the mouth, who draw in the streams of doctrine spiritually, and yet do not bend in carnal fashion to perverse works. In the trumpets is the cry of the preachings; in the lamps the brightness of the miracles; in the pitchers the frailty of bodies. For our leader led such with him to the battle of preaching as, despising the safety of their bodies, would lay low the enemies by dying, and would overcome their swords not with arms but with patience. For our martyrs came armed to the battle under their leader, namely with trumpets, pitchers and lamps: they sound with trumpets while they preach; they break the pitchers while they set their bodies, to be dissolved in suffering, against the swords of the enemy; they shine with the lamps while after the dissolution of their bodies they flash with miracles. And at once the enemies are turned to flight, because when they see the bodies of the dead martyrs flash with miracles, broken by the light of truth they believed what they were assailing. They sounded the trumpets, then, that the pitchers might be broken; the pitchers were broken that the lamps might appear; the lamps appeared that the enemies might be turned to flight; that is, the martyrs preached until their bodies were dissolved; these were dissolved that they might flash with miracles; they flashed that they might lay the enemies low by the divine light, lest, standing up, they should resist God, and that, made subject, they might fear him. And it is to be noted that the enemies stood before the pitchers but fled the lamps, because the persecutors of the faith resisted the preachers while they were still in the body; but after the dissolution of their bodies, when the miracles appeared, they were turned to flight, because, terrified with dread, they ceased from the persecution of the faithful: namely, by the preaching of the trumpets, the pitchers of the bodies being broken, they feared, having seen the lamps of the miracles. It is to be noted too that it is written there that they held the trumpets in the right hand and the pitchers in the left. For we are said to hold as on the right whatever we weigh as great, and as on the left what [we weigh] as nothing. Well, then, did they hold the trumpets in the right hand and the pitchers in the left, because the martyrs of Christ hold the glory of preaching as great, but the profit of their bodies as least. But whoever makes more of the profit of the body than of the grace of preaching holds the trumpet in the left hand and the pitcher in the right.

09_marg263: AND THEY BROKE THEIR PITCHERS. ADAMANTIUS. They carry pitchers and lamps and a horn trumpet in their hands, and so they come to that innumerable multitude of enemies, among whom were camels like the sand of the sea. And when they had come to the battle they sounded the horn trumpets, and let the pitchers fall from their hands, and they were broken. Then, seizing the lamps, they rush upon the adversaries and at the same time blow the trumpets. See how the chosen soldiers of God fight with lamps. For so Christ had armed them, saying: "Let your loins be girt, and lamps burning in your hands"; and: So let your light shine before men, that they may see your good works, etc. With such lamps lit, then, the soldiers of Christ ought to fight, shining with the light of works. And he sounds the trumpet who speaks of heavenly things, discourses of spiritual things, and reveals the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven. He speaks with a trumpet who [speaks] of great and greatest things, who opens the knowledge of Christ to human ears. And the trumpet is called of horn because it is said of the saint: "His horn shall be exalted in glory." Therefore the trumpet of each is called of horn, because it discourses of the manifold knowledge of Christ and the sacraments of his cross, which is signified in the horn. With this trumpet, then, serving and fighting, we conquer the foreigners and turn the enemies to flight, even if their multitude be like the locusts. For the multitude of the demons is compared to locusts, which have a seat neither in heaven nor on earth. Let there go before, then, in this war the light of works and of knowledge, virtue, the preaching of the divine word. Let us too fight, singing together in hymns and psalms and spiritual canticles and crying to the Lord, that we may merit to obtain the victory from him.
09_marg264: AND GEDEON MADE THEREOF. AUGUSTINE. It is asked what the ephud or ephot is. If indeed it is a priestly vestment, as most say, or rather an over-vestment, which in Greek is called ependyma or epomis, which may better be understood as the superhumeral, it rightly perplexes one how Gedeon made it of so much gold. For it is written: And the weight of the golden earrings which he had asked was a thousand seven hundred sicles of gold, besides the bracelets and collars and purple coverings which were upon the kings of Madian, besides the collars that were on the necks of the camels; and Gedeon made it into an ephud, and set it up in his city, and all Israel went a whoring after it, etc. How, then, could this garment be made of so much gold? For the mother of Samuel too made him an ephud bad, which indeed they have translated a linen ephud, when she gave him to the Lord to be brought up in the temple; where it appears more evidently that this is a kind of vestment. Or is it said, he set it up in his city, so that it might be understood that it was made of gold? For it is not said placed, but set up, because it was so solid that it could be set up, that is, being placed, it stood. When Gedeon, then, had done this unlawful thing, all Israel went a whoring after it, that is, by following it against the law of God.
09_marg265: Whence it is not idly asked, since it was not an idol, that is, the image of some false god, but an ephud, that is, one of the sacraments of the tabernacle, which belonged to the priestly vesture, how the Scripture speaks of the fornication of the people venerating these things. It is because, namely, apart from the tabernacle of God, where were those things which God had commanded to be made there, it was not lawful for anything like them to be made outside. Therefore it became a scandal to Gedeon and his house, that is, so that he departed from God, whom he had offended; because this too was a certain kind of idol, that anything made with hands should be worshipped as God outside the tabernacle of God, since those very things which were commanded to be made in the tabernacle were referred rather to the worship of God than worshipped as God or as the image of God.
09_marg266: Although by the ephud, in that manner of speech which signifies the whole by a part, all the things can be understood which Gedeon set up in his city, as for the worship of God, like the tabernacle of God; and so by the ephot, because this is the mark of the priestly honour; so that the sin of Gedeon would be this, that outside the tabernacle of God he made something like it, where God might be worshipped: not that he set up an ephud of solid gold as if to be adored, but that of that gold he made the things which belonged to the ornaments or instruments of the sanctuary, all of which are signified by the ephud. The ephud itself too was not commanded to be made of gold alone; but this is the superhumeral of the priestly vesture, and it has something of gold. For it was commanded to be made of gold and hyacinth and purple and scarlet and fine linen. But because the Seventy set these things down in such a way that, having mentioned all that Gedeon had received of the spoils, they add: and Gedeon made it into an ephud, it seems that this was made of the whole of it; whereas by that manner of speech which signifies a part by the whole it can be understood thus: he made it into an ephud, as if, "thence he made an ephud", or "of it he made an ephud", not, namely, using all of it up on the ephud, but spending of it as much as was sufficient. For in that translation which is from the Hebrew it is read thus: And Gedeon made an ephod thereof. For what among the Seventy is ephut is read in the Hebrew ephot. But not all the priests used such a superhumeral, which was of gold, hyacinth, purple, scarlet and fine linen, but only the high priest. That, then, which was given to Samuel by his mother while he was still a boy was not such; whence it is called ephut bad, that is, linen. But I think Gedeon made that which was the chief vestment of the priest, by which the other works of the sanctuary too were signified, which he set up in his city apart from the tabernacle of God. And therefore it became a scandal to him and his house, so that his numerous offspring of sons perished, as the Scripture afterwards testifies.
09_marg267: AUGUSTINE. It is to be understood that it was said by prolepsis that Gedeon made an ephot against the law of God of the gold which had been taken from the conquered enemies, so that it might be said at once whence the gold was and what was made of it. For this sin was committed at the end of the days of Gedeon, when the evils followed which the Scripture joins on, after it has said for how many years the land rested in the days of Gedeon.
09_marg268: BUT AFTER [GEDEON] WAS DEAD. AUGUSTINE. And it came to pass, when Gedeon was dead, that the children of Israel turned away, and went a whoring after Baalim, and they set up for themselves Baalberith as a covenant, that he should be their god, etc. Both Baalim and Baalberith are to be understood as idols. The transgression and fornication of the people after the death of Gedeon, then, is greater than while he lived, apart from the ephut; which, even if it was done unlawfully, was yet of the sacraments of the tabernacle; but this idolatry has not even a false defence of their fathers' religion. Whence, even if the ephut was made at the end of the time of Gedeon, yet before this God bore with it so patiently that peace continued in the land; because, though what he had forbidden had been done, yet he had not gone far from him who had commanded something of the kind to be made in his tabernacle in his honour. But now he would not have the graver things committed, and the open fornication of the people after idols, go unpunished.
